verdicts.reason: Without the async reset at line 64, pwm_sync_d keeps tracking pwm_sync during reset (or stays X if no clock ran), instead of being forced to 0. If pwm_sync was 1 at the last edge before reset is released and is 0 at the first edge after, pwm_fall fires and the counter at line 140 advances one extra time, so PGOOD asserts a cycle earlier.

With the reset assignment deleted, pwm_sync_d holds its value from before reset (X at power-up). A held 1 gives a pwm_fall pulse at the first edge after reset if pwm_sync is low, which advances qualify_counter (line 140) one extra time and moves PGOOD's assertion earlier.

Resetting pwm_sync_d to 1 makes pwm_fall (line 89) pulse at the first edge after reset whenever pwm_sync is low. If run_active and pgood_comp are high, that pulse gives one extra count, so PGOOD asserts one switching cycle earlier.

pwm_sync_d is frozen while run_active is low. At the first edge with run_active high, pwm_fall at line 89 compares the live pwm_sync with a stale sample, so it can produce a spurious count or miss a real one. That shifts when qualify_counter reaches TARGET and so when PGOOD rises.
With pwm_sync_d stuck at 1, pwm_fall at line 89 becomes ~pwm_sync. The counter then advances on every clock that PWM is low instead of once per cycle, so PGOOD asserts far sooner.
pwm_fall becomes ~pwm_sync(previous) & ~pwm_sync, which is high on every clock where PWM has been low for two samples. The count rate changes, and so does PGOOD timing.

A registered pwm_fall lags by one clock and has no reset value. Line 124 is evaluated against the same-clock run_active and pgood_comp, so a delayed pulse can land on a clock where the clear condition holds (or not) differently than in the original, which changes the count. PGOOD timing changes, and an X after reset is also possible.
XOR fires on both PWM edges, so qualify_counter advances twice per switching cycle and PGOOD asserts in roughly half the qualifying time.

Counting on rising edges instead of falling edges moves each increment by the PWM high time. A pgood_comp dip or a run_active drop between the two edges then gives a different count, and the final increment (and PGOOD rise) lands on a different clock.
~pwm_sync_d & ~pwm_sync is high on every clock that PWM stays low. The counter advances many times per cycle and PGOOD asserts much earlier.
The inverted pwm_fall is high on almost every clock except the falling edge. The counter then advances nearly every clock and PGOOD timing changes drastically.
pwm_fall = pwm_sync_d is high on every clock after PWM has been high, so the counter at line 140 advances many times per switching cycle instead of once.
pwm_sync_d | ~pwm_sync is high on most clocks, so the counter advances far more often than once per cycle and PGOOD asserts early.
pwm_sync_d & pwm_sync is high on every clock that PWM stays high, so the count rate changes and PGOOD asserts at a different time.

Without the async reset, qualify_counter is not cleared by rst_n and starts as X. If the counter was at TARGET and reset is asserted while run_active and pgood_comp are high (not ruled out by the header), PGOOD at line 169 stays 1 instead of 0.

With the reset assignment deleted, qualify_counter holds its value through reset. A counter at TARGET with run_active and pgood_comp high keeps PGOOD (line 169) high during and after reset, and the power-up value is X.
Resetting the counter to 1 means it reaches TARGET (4050) one pwm_fall sooner after reset, so PGOOD asserts one switching cycle early.
When pwm_fall coincides with pgood_comp or run_active being low, the counter increments instead of clearing. The good-cycle run is no longer required to be consecutive, so PGOOD can assert earlier.
With the condition always true, the first pwm_fall loads TARGET directly, so PGOOD asserts after one good cycle instead of 4050.

This branch runs only when qualify_counter == TARGET (line 132), so the deleted line wrote TARGET into a register that already holds TARGET. Without it, the register keeps the same value, and nothing else in the module depends on the assignment.
Counting down from 0 wraps to 4095 (12-bit counter) and reaches TARGET = 4050 after 46 pwm_fall pulses instead of 4050, so PGOOD asserts far earlier.
